about: Planted case and truth for the case study 'The name nobody wrote down', by acceptance/cases/unwritten-name/make.py. All content is fictional.

story.title: The name nobody wrote down
story.puzzle: Dana Kovar, a nurse, boarded the last bus out of Wenmere on Saturday 14 March 2026 and never reached her night shift in Holt Cross. The bus company's gate log, fuel receipts and dispatch sheet run to several hundred lines over five months, and nobody reading them saw anything wrong.
story.twist: Aron Vesk, who drove her bus, is named in every log until that night and in none for the next 73 days, though the roster kept him on route 9 and the gate line for his last run was left blank. The gap finder sets his silence beside the day Dana was last seen; a person decides what it means.

acts.title: A nurse does not reach her night shift
acts.story: Dana Kovar left her flat in Wenmere for the 22:40 bus to Holt Cross on Saturday 14 March and never reached the clinic. Her flatmate's statement, the missing person notice and her photograph arrive; the analyst joins the three papers about her as one person.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: The night supervisor saw her board
acts.story: The station's night supervisor says she showed Dana to stand 3 and saw her board the 22:40, driven by Aron Vesk. Her signed statement is a scanned page, read by the OCR tool from its fixed text. The gate book page for that night and a photograph of the depot yard come with it; the gate line for bus 14 at 22:41 has no driver.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: Who drives route 9
acts.story: The depot manager writes that the route 9 lates are Aron Vesk's duty on bus 14, and sends the roster. The intake brief reads the first three papers together.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: The depot's logs to the end of March
acts.story: Ostry Coaches hands over the gate log and fuel receipts for February and March and the March dispatch sheet: several hundred lines, each driver named by initial and surname or by fuel card. Each line is its own mention, joined to its driver. Aron Vesk's last named line is 12 March.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: A standing question on the driver
acts.story: The analyst asks the case to tell her when Aron Vesk is named in a new record. Its first check reads what the case already holds: the papers that name him up to 12 March and the night of the 14th.

steps.question: Tell me when Aron Vesk is named in a new record.

acts.title: April's logs, and nothing on him
acts.story: The April gate log and fuel receipts arrive, with a police charge sheet and a bail record about two other drivers. The question wakes on the new lines and finds no record naming him: his late duty goes out every working day under relief.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: May and June: his name is back
acts.story: The logs for May and June arrive. The question wakes again and reports the new gate log and fuel receipts that name him, from 26 May.

steps.why: the logs name a driver by initial and surname, and the depot manager says who drives each route and bus; one driver in every paper

acts.title: Seventy-three days with no name
acts.story: The gap finder sets the supervisor's last sight of Aron Vesk on 14 March beside his next named log line on 26 May: no record of him for 73 days. It also flags that nothing places Dana Kovar after that night. It proposes; a person decides what the silence means.

acts.title: Who was at the depot that night
acts.story: The analyst checks the log lines for 14 March against the gate book page and accepts them with the two last-seen accounts. Discovery proposes the people placed at the coach station that day. The gate times show the early drivers gone by 14:15, so she keeps Dana Kovar, Aron Vesk and Leon Abbot, the late driver in the yard until 23:53, and accepts it as an incident. The same set read as people together says nothing more, and she rejects it.

steps.why: checked against the gate book page for 14 March

incident.title: Dana Kovar boards the 22:40 to Holt Cross at Wenmere coach station

steps.reject: Every driver on shift is at the depot each day; being there together says nothing more. The incident keeps who was there that evening.

acts.title: A colleague works the lead
acts.story: The analyst assigns the May and June gate log and the gate book page to a colleague and asks her whether the driver named on 26 May is the Aron Vesk of the 22:40. She answers on the line and marks her work updated.

steps.why: Is this the Aron Vesk who drove the 22:40 on 14 March?

steps.text: Yes. Bus 14 on route 9 lates, his duty before the night, and the roster still lists him. His fuel card is used again from the same week.

acts.title: The conclusion
acts.story: The analyst writes what the case shows: a lead, not a finding about what he did. She cites the two sightings and his last and next log lines, sets aside leave and missed entries, names what is not established, and signs; a reviewer agrees.
